Humaiun: No scope for Bangladesh to join BRICS Summit; PM wasn’t invited
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday said there is scope for Bangladesh to send a government representative to the BRICS Summit, as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was not invited to the summit and the invitation was instead extended to the BIMSTEC Chair.
“How shall we go? Has anyone from the Bangladesh government been invited? Our prime minister was not invited. Who told you that our prime minister was invited? The BIMSTEC Chair was invited. Then why are you asking this question?” he told reporters ruling out the possibility of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman attending the BRICS Summit.
Responding to a question at the Foreign Service Academy, Kobir said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s first visit to India cannot be a multilateral visit.
He said the government is working on arranging a bilateral visit to India when the timing is conducive.
In April 2025, Bangladesh assumed the chairmanship of the regional grouping - Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) - for the next two years, reaffirming its commitment to advancing regional cooperation and development.
BIMSTEC consists of seven member countries, namely Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
India confirmed that an invitation was extended to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to attend the BRICS Summit as the BIMSTEC Chair, as a separate bilateral invitation has been in place since February this year.
BRICS member States and United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres will attend the 18th BRICS Summit to be held in New Delhi, India, on September 12-13.
The United Nations India confirmed his participation in a post on its verified Facebook page on Wednesday.
As BRICS Chair 2026, India will be hosting the 18th BRICS Summit at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.
The Summit will bring together leaders of BRICS member and partner countries as well as outreach invitees.
India’s BRICS Chairship is guided by the theme: “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, reflecting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a people-centric approach rooted in the spirit of "Humanity First."
In addition to these areas, the leaders will exchange views on strengthening intra-BRICS cooperation on common priorities and share perspectives on global and regional matters of mutual importance.
Under India’s Chairship this year, over 350 meetings and high-level engagements have been held in over 25 cities across India to further strengthen the BRICS strategic partnership across three fundamental pillars: political and security, economic and financial, and cultural and people-to-people exchanges, said the host country.
Through these engagements, and business-to-business and people-to-people initiatives, India's BRICS Chairship has contributed to advancing BRICS cooperation through practical and development-oriented outcomes.
India is a founding member of BRICS, and has previously held its Chairship three times in 2012, 2016 and 2021. India assumed its fourth BRICS Chairship on 1 January 2026.
The year 2026 also marks a significant milestone as BRICS completes 20 years since its establishment.

item.title: Thakurgaon-1 by-polls on October 29
item.description:
The Election Commission has announced October 29 for the by-election to the Thakurgaon-1 constituency, three weeks after Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected president.
Election Commission Secretary Akhtar Ahmed announced the schedule on Thursday after the commission, led by Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, finalised it.
According to the schedule, the deadline for submitting nomination papers is September 27, with scrutiny set for September 29. Candidates can withdraw their nominations until October 7, while electoral symbols will be allocated on October 8.
Voting will be held from 8am to 4pm without a break, Akhtar said at a briefing at the Election Commission headquarters.
The Thakurgaon district election officer has been appointed returning officer, with three assistant returning officers.
Mirza Fakhrul was elected president through a parliamentary vote on August 20 and took the oath the following day. The Parliament Secretariat subsequently declared his Thakurgaon-1 seat vacant.

item.title: Humaiun: Global community must act to resolve Rohingya crisis
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday called on the international community to move beyond expressions of solidarity and ensure shared responsibility and sustained political engagement to resolve the Rohingya crisis.
“Nine years of displacement should not make displacement acceptable. It should make finding a solution more urgent than ever on this crisis,” Kobir said while speaking at a program at the Foreign Service Academy.
Bangladesh has hosted Rohingya refugees for decades and, particularly since the massive influx in 2017, has provided refuge and protection to more than one million forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals.
“We have done so despite the considerable pressure this has placed on our economy, environment, public services, local communities and national security,” Kobir said.
He said Bangladesh has demonstrated “humanitarian responsibility and humanitarian leadership,” but such responsibility must not be mistaken for unlimited responsibility.
“Let me be clear: this is not a crisis that Bangladesh created, and it cannot be a crisis that Bangladesh resolves alone,” the state minister said.
Humanitarian financing, he said, must remain predictable and consistent, while host communities must receive meaningful support.
Regional cooperation must be structured, and every engagement with Myanmar must remain focused on addressing the conditions that produced this displacement in the very first place, Kobir said.
He also underscored the distinction between humanitarian assistance and a political solution.
“Humanitarian assistance manages the consequences of displacement. Only a political solution can end displacement,” he said.
Kobir said the objective remains clear: the safe, voluntary, dignified and sustainable return of the Rohingya to Myanmar.
“But return must not simply mean crossing a border. It must mean returning to a place where people can live with security, rights, dignity and confidence in their future,” he said.
That, he added, requires conditions and an environment that make the return of the Rohingya genuinely sustainable.
The state minister said the crisis also demands a broader regional approach, with ASEAN playing an important role alongside the United Nations and regional countries.
“We need a comprehensive approach that connects humanitarian action with diplomacy, accountability, development, resource mobilisation and political dialogue,” he said.
Kobir said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has taken a decisive step towards addressing the matter by establishing the National Strategy Formulation Committee on the Rohingya issue.
“It will not be just another committee. It brings together, for the first time, diplomatic, humanitarian and security institutions under a comprehensive framework,” he said.
Addressing young diplomats and students present at the event, Kobir said diplomacy is not simply the art of managing difficult situations.
“At its best, diplomacy is the art of creating possibilities when none appear to exist,” he said.
“The Rohingya crisis will test precisely that capacity. Our responsibility is not merely to manage another year of displacement. Our responsibility is to create political conditions in which another decade of displacement becomes unnecessary. We will do our utmost,” he said.
Kobir said Bangladesh, as the country presiding over the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, would seek to keep the Rohingya crisis high on the agenda of the UN and other multilateral platforms.
“We will work with our bilateral partners to create an enabling environment, raise the profile of the Rohingya crisis and mobilise the international financial support that is required to resolve this crisis,” he said.
Bangladesh, under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, will work with important stakeholders, including China, and engage with the government of Myanmar and other relevant parties to find a peaceful and sustainable resolution to the crisis, he said.
“I hope today’s discussion will contribute not only to a better understanding of the crisis but also to evolving a coherent strategy, and most importantly, to resolving this crisis,” Kobir said.

item.title: Yemen rebels report about 40 Saudi strikes in fresh attack
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels reported about 40 airstrikes launched by Saudi forces on Thursday in a fresh salvo following attacks by the Iran-backed group against the kingdom.
“The Saudi enemy’s air force conducted around 40 strikes in recent hours in the governorates of Taiz, Hodeida, Al-Jawf and Marib,” Houthi news agency Saba said.
The Houthis, who control large parts of northwest Yemen, launched a large-scale offensive last week against Yemeni government forces, who are backed by Saudi Arabia.
They also launched attacks on Saudi territory that left dozens wounded.
On Wednesday the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said the rebels fired ballistic missiles and drones at several cities in southern Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi civil defense issued alerts warning of “potential danger” in two areas, Khamis Mushait and Abha.
The Houthis are seeking to advance towards coastal areas of the Red Sea that border the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key shipping lane.
The waterway, which links Asia to Europe via the Red Sea and Suez Canal, has gained importance as a transit route since the start of the wider Middle East war, which saw Iran blockade the Strait of Hormuz.
Since last week, the fighting in Yemen has left more than 500 dead, mostly combatants, according to an AFP tally compiled from several sources.
The country relapsed into war in July after years of calm, drawn into the regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli offensive against Iran that began at the end of February.
